Chapter 7: OM and the Yogic Path—Integrating with Other Techniques
When it comes to the world of yoga and meditation, OM isn’t just an isolated practice. It’s actually woven into a much bigger tapestry, connecting with so many other techniques along the yogic path. And when you start blending OM with these different tools, you’ll notice the experience gets richer, the benefits deeper—a truly holistic approach to your own well-being and self-discovery.
Let’s talk about one of the most natural ways to integrate OM: with asana, or yoga postures. Imagine chanting OM right before you start your session. It instantly centers your mind and gets your body ready for movement. Some people even like to chant OM at the start of each posture, letting the sound guide their breath and movement. It’s like every pose transforms into an expression of OM’s underlying vibration—a seamless flow connecting mind, body, and sound.
Now, if you’re into pranayama—that’s breath control—OM pairs beautifully here too. Picture yourself practicing alternate nostril breathing, or nadi shodhana, and then finishing with a few rounds of OM chanting. The breath acts as a bridge, linking the physical and subtle bodies, while OM draws your awareness into the present moment. The result? A balanced nervous system and a much deeper sense of relaxation.
OM also works hand-in-hand with mantra meditation. You can combine OM with other mantras, like OM Shanti or OM Namah Shivaya, either as a prefix or on its own. When you add OM, it amplifies the mantra’s effect, grounding it in that universal vibration. It’s like giving your meditation an extra boost of energy and focus.
Even mindfulness and loving-kindness practices can be enhanced with OM. Try silently repeating OM while you’re sending kind thoughts to yourself—or to others. It’s a simple way to deepen your sense of connection and compassion, making those moments feel even more meaningful.
So, how do you bring all these elements together? Here’s a simple framework you might try:
Start by chanting OM to center your mind and set an intention.
Move into your asana practice or pranayama, using breath and body to get ready for deeper meditation.
Transition into silent OM meditation, letting the sound gently fade into stillness.
And finally, close your practice by chanting OM or a related mantra, sealing everything with a sense of unity and peace.
By weaving OM throughout your practice, it becomes both the foundation and the connecting thread—tying together all the different aspects of the yogic journey. What you’re left with is a practice that feels both grounded and expansive. It’s rooted in tradition, yet flexible enough to adapt to your own needs. And that’s the beauty of integrating OM with the yogic path.
